claim: CTCF ChIP-seq signal overlaps the CACNA1B e37a locus in approximately 50% of human cell lines (27 of 50).
source: We observed a robust chromatin immunoprecipitation followed by sequencing (ChIP-seq) signal for the zinc finger DNA binding protein CCCTC-binding factor (CTCF) that overlaps the CACNA1B e37a locus in ~50% of human cell lines (27 of 50; 9 of 50 tracks are shown in Figure 1B; ENCODE Project Consortium, 2012).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by analysis of ENCODE ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: None of the 50 human cell line tracks contained a ChIP-seq CTCF signal associated with CACNA1B e37b.
source: None of the 50 tracks contained a ChIP-seq CTCF signal associated with CACNA1B e37b (Figure 1B).
evidence: The claim is explicitly stated in the text and supported by the ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Mouse Cacna1b e37a and e37b share 60% nucleotide identity.
source: and it associates with mouse Cacna1b e37a but not e37b, which share 60% nucleotide identity (Figure 2A and B).
evidence: The claim is explicitly stated in the text and supported by sequence comparison shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Recombinant CTCF binds to an e37a-containing DNA probe in a concentration-dependent manner.
source: Recombinant CTCF bound to an e37a-containing DNA probe in a concentration manner (Figure 2B)
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by gel shift assay data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: CTCF failed to bind an e37a-containing RNA probe.
source: but CTCF failed to bind an e37a-containing RNA probe (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is explicitly stated and supported by RNA gel shift assay data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: CTCF binds with high specificity to Cacna1b e37a but not Cacna1b e37b.
source: Based on the following observations we conclude that CTCF binds with high specificity to Cacna1b e37a but not Cacna1b e37b: 1) CTCF bound e37a but not e37b DNA probes when studied using the same conditions (Figure 2C and D; compare lanes 2 and 6); 2) the appearance of a third super-shifted band when e37a probe is incubated with both recombinant CTCF and a CTCF monoclonal antibody (Figure 2C and D; lane 3); 3) total displacement of CTCF binding from the labeled e37a DNA probe on addition of unlabeled e37a DNA probe (Figure 2C and D; lane 4); and CTCF binding to e37a DNA is concentration dependent (Figure 2B).
evidence: The claim is explicitly stated as a conclusion and supported by multiple lines of experimental evidence from gel shift assays shown in Figures 2B, 2C, and 2D.

claim: CTCF is localized to cell nuclei in F11 cells.
source: CTCF is localized to cell nuclei in F11 cells (Figure 3A).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by fluorescence microscopy images in Figure 3A.

claim: CTCF binds Cacna1b e37a locus in F11 cells based on CTCF ChIP-qPCR.
source: We found that CTCF binds Cacna1b e37a locus in F11 cells based on CTCF ChIP-qPCR (Figure 3B).
evidence: The claim is explicitly stated and supported by ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: CTCF does not bind e37b locus in F11 cells.
source: By contrast, CTCF does not bind e37b locus (Figure 3B).
evidence: The claim is explicitly stated and supported by ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Overexpression of recombinant CTCF tagged with GFP induced approximately 2-fold increase in Cacna1b e37a levels within 2 days of cDNA transfection in F11 cells.

evidence: The claim is explicitly stated and supported by Western blot and qRT-PCR data shown in Figures 3D and 3E.

claim: siRNA targeting Ctcf in F11 cells reduced levels of e37a-containing Cacna1b mRNAs by approximately 30% 3 days after transfection.
source: siRNA targeting Ctcf in F11 cells (Figure 3F and G) had the expected opposite effect; levels of e37a-containing Cacna1b mRNAs were ~30% reduced 3 days after transfecting Ctcf siRNA relative to control siRNA (Figure 3G).
evidence: The claim is explicitly stated and supported by Western blot and qRT-PCR data shown in Figures 3F and 3G.

claim: CTCF promotes e37a inclusion in Cacna1b mRNAs.

evidence: The claim is explicitly stated as a conclusion based on the overexpression and knockdown experiments.

claim: CTCF levels are rate limiting for Cacna1b e37a splicing in neuronal cells.

evidence: The claim is explicitly stated as a conclusion based on the overexpression and knockdown experiments showing dose-dependent effects.

claim: CTCF binding to gDNA is inhibited by 5-methylcytosine (5-mC) within the CTCF binding motif.
